detailedExplanation: This topic is verified against The Tiffin Girls’ School Year 9 Biology Curriculum Outline 2026–27 and the corresponding AQA GCSE Biology 8461 content.

DNA is the molecule that carries genetic information. In eukaryotic cells, DNA is arranged into chromosomes inside the nucleus. A gene is a small section of DNA that codes for a sequence of amino acids used to make a particular protein. The genome is the entire genetic material of an organism.
DNA is a polymer made from two strands arranged in a double helix. Each strand is built from repeating nucleotides. Each nucleotide contains: - a sugar; - a phosphate group; and - one base.

There are four DNA bases: A, C, G and T. The sugar and phosphate form the alternating backbone of each strand. The order of the bases carries genetic information. A sequence of three bases codes for an amino acid, and the order of bases therefore determines the order of amino acids in a protein.

Understanding the human genome can help scientists identify genes linked to disease, understand inherited disorders and investigate human migration/evolution.

additionalSourceSections.heading: Revision map
additionalSourceSections.body:
Largest to smaller context: cell → nucleus → chromosome → DNA → gene
A gene is a section of DNA; a chromosome contains many genes.
DNA bases: A adenine · C cytosine · G guanine · T thymine.
